clue.text: Ducks answer, bound by unions

indicators.note: bound by means held in on both sides, so the unions word wraps round the answer piece

parts.note: unions of companies are mergers

explanation.surface: Some ducks reply while tied up in trade union business.
explanation.definitionFit: These are fish-eating diving birds with saw-edged bills, a kind of duck.

clue.text: Maybe gutted, having trouble with field

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Someone is possibly devastated, struggling with a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassy land kept for hay or grazing is a field.

clue.text: Repercussion as place found in mature surroundings

indicators.note: found in means located within, so the place letters go inside the mature word
surroundings says the mature word forms the outside around the place letters

parts.note: ripe means mature

explanation.surface: An effect of something happening in a grown-up setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A spreading effect or consequence following an event is a repercussion.

clue.text: That may be so loaded long wall collapsed

indicators.note: collapsed means fallen into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Perhaps so, but the long wall carrying a load fell down.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase grants a point is fine in itself, usually before a 'but', like saying perhaps so.

clue.text: Gulped, seeing son and wife given permission

parts.note: allowed means given permission

explanation.surface: A family member gulps, noticing his parents have been allowed something.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gulped something down is to have taken it into the throat quickly.

clue.text: Moore perhaps understood and agreed

definitions.meaning: the actor Moore who played James Bond had this first name
in radio talk this word means message received and understood

explanation.surface: A man named Moore grasped the point and said yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators say this to confirm they have received a message; Moore the actor bore this first name.

clue.text: Quiet expression of sympathy for old ruler

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
ah is a sound of sympathy

explanation.surface: Someone hushes a crowd while sighing sympathetically for a deposed monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The title belonged to the monarchs of Iran before the 1979 revolution, hence an old ruler.

clue.text: Hussar, say, may see hard Viking losing head

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a Viking was a Norseman

explanation.surface: A cavalryman may meet a tough Viking who is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar was a light cavalry soldier, an example of a mounted rider.

clue.text: Tourist disposing of old hat for farmworker

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of, so these letters are taken out of the tourist word

parts.note: a tourist is a holidaymaker
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A visitor throws away a worn-out hat to work on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who cuts and dries grass for fodder is a farm labourer.

clue.text: No abusive cop is possibly considered blameless

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A police officer who never mistreats people is deemed beyond reproach.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone regarded as above doubt or guilt is considered blameless.

clue.text: Horrify a mate, eating prawn's head

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so the prawn's initial goes into the a-mate pair

parts.note: a mate is a pal

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A friend is disgusted to see someone biting a prawn's head off.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay or shock someone greatly is to horrify them.

clue.text: Dispute book kept by Gray twice revised

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the book letter sits within the repeated name
twice means the rearranged name is used two times over
revised means the letters of the name are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A literary quarrel over a book that Gray edited two times.
explanation.walkthrough: Gray, rearranged by 'revised', gives ARGY; 'twice' makes ARGYARGY, and B goes into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal British term means a noisy quarrel or squabbling row.

clue.text: Blair, the writer, has Independent line for right source of energy

indicators.note: for means one piece goes in place of another, the Independent and line letters replacing right

parts.note: Eric Blair wrote as George Orwell

explanation.surface: An author named Blair joins the Independent newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Orwell's real name was Eric Arthur Blair, so the surface wants the politician Tony Blair but means the novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: A drilled hole yielding petroleum supplies fuel, a source of energy.

clue.text: The Seine perhaps covers one area that's part of the South of France

definitions.text: part of the South of France

indicators.note: covers means wraps round, so the river word goes around the numeral one

parts.note: the Seine is an example of a river
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A French river flows over a region in the south of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Côte d'Azur coastline of southern France is known by this name.

clue.text: A lot led astray holding anarchic views must be a myth

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one rearrangement sits inside the other
astray means gone wrong, so these letters are scrambled
anarchic means disordered, so these letters are scrambled too

explanation.surface: Many people led off course by wild opinions must be believing a fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' turns A LOT LED into OLDTALE; 'anarchic' turns VIEWS into WIVES, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstition handed down by folk tradition is a popular but false belief.

clue.text: Love tuna cooked and filled with very little pastry

indicators.note: filled with means having something put inside, so V goes into the rearranged letters
cooked means prepared in a new way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: V is a small abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A tuna lover makes a small filled pastry case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns LOVE TUNA into VOLAUENT, and V goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small round case of puff pastry with a savoury filling.

clue.text: Candidate or worker after seeing hope curtailed

indicators.note: after means the worker piece comes behind the shortened word
curtailed means cut short, so the last letter of the hope word is dropped

parts.note: to aspire is to hope
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A job applicant or employee whose hopes have been cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone striving for a position or office is a candidate for it.

clue.text: Voice that sings of wrong exaggerated uprising

parts.note: false means wrong

indicators.note: in a down clue uprising means read upwards, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means exaggerated

explanation.surface: A singer tells of a false, overblown rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: A male singing register above the normal range is a type of singing voice.

clue.text: Reworked last design as feature of church

indicators.note: reworked means done again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An earlier design was redone to become part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured windows depicting saints are a typical decorative element of churches.

clue.text: Language of love in southern African country

indicators.note: in places the love letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Romance in a southern African nation, described in its tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Cushitic tongue spoken in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Province of politician in Ireland

indicators.note: in places the politician letters inside the Ireland word

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A region governed by a politician in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A province can mean a sphere of control or a domain, as can a realm ruled by one power.

clue.text: On air, encourage understanding

indicators.note: on air means broadcast, so heard rather than read, signalling a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to encourage someone to act is to incite them

explanation.surface: A broadcaster urges listeners towards understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep perception of a situation is a form of understanding.

clue.text: Part of body with temperature above normal?

parts.note: high means above the normal level

explanation.surface: A body part running a fever?
explanation.definitionFit: The upper leg between hip and knee is a part of the body.

clue.text: Current model chasing a French dress

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so the current and model pieces follow the French article

parts.note: un is French for a
I is the symbol for electric current
a form is a model or pattern

explanation.surface: A fashion model hurries after a French dress currently in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard clothing worn by a group, such as soldiers, is a kind of dress.

clue.text: Writer is free at last, okay

parts.note: a writer is an author

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word free

explanation.surface: A writer is finally released, and all is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To okay something is to sanction or approve it officially.

clue.text: A quip oddly used by Irish national

indicators.note: used by means the picked letters are taken up by the Irish abbreviation, which leads
oddly means the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, are taken

explanation.surface: An Irishman makes a strange joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A national here is a citizen of a country, in this case Iraq.

clue.text: Four of these may be found in eight

definitions.text: Four of these may be found in eight

parts.words: Four of these may be found in eight
parts.note: eight divided into pairs gives four of them, as eight equals four times two

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what fits four times into eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Two goes into eight four times, so eight holds four of the number.

clue.text: Jumbled sound waves?

parts.note: random sound containing all frequencies at once is like a muddle of waves

explanation.surface: A question about scrambled sound waves.
explanation.definitionFit: This is random noise with equal intensity across frequencies, a jumble of sound.
